meta.title: Velox — a native UI framework for Rust
meta.description: Velox is a modular Rust UI framework: a single-file-component compiler, a layout engine, a CSS cascade and a Skia renderer that paint straight to the screen. No browser, no DOM, no runtime.
meta.ogAlt: The Velox homepage: a Rust UI framework rendering to a Skia raster surface

install.title: Install the CLI
install.description: Velox ships as a cargo binary. Build it from source, or install it into your cargo bin directory.
install.fromSource: From a clone of the repository

hero.lede: Velox compiles Vue-like components to Rust, runs a real layout engine, resolves a CSS cascade, and rasterizes through Skia. No browser. No DOM. No webview. Just a tree, a layout pass, and pixels on a surface you own.

pipeline.title: One frame, end to end
pipeline.description: A signal changes. Everything below re-runs on the next frame — there is no retained tree to diff against, because there is no tree to retain.

signal.name: Signal
signal.desc: State changes; dependent effects are queued.

render.name: Render
render.desc: The generated render() builds a fresh VNode tree.

style.name: Resolve style
style.desc: The stylesheet resolves onto the tree. Last match wins.

layout.name: Layout
layout.desc: Block and flex layout compute geometry for the viewport.

paint.name: Paint
paint.desc: Skia rasterizes into a reused surface, then presents.

pipeline.note: Every stage runs from scratch on every frame. Nothing is diffed against the previous frame.

features.title: What Velox is
features.description: The parts that exist today, measured from the source rather than from the roadmap.

sfc.title: Single-file components
sfc.body: A .vx file holds a template, a script setup block and a style block. velox-sfc parses it and generates plain Rust render functions — no runtime compiler, no eval, nothing interpreted at run time.

reactivity.title: Signals and effects
reactivity.body: Signal, effect, computed, watch and next_tick cover the reactive primitives. State is Rc<Signal<T>>, which makes it !Send by construction: Velox is one thread per window, on purpose.

layout.title: A real layout engine
layout.body: Block and flexbox layout, margins and padding, intrinsic and constrained sizing, absolute and fixed positioning, z-index and stacking contexts, overflow clipping and scroll offsets.

style.title: A CSS cascade
style.body: Around 120 properties, descendant and attribute selectors, and inline style synthesis. There is no specificity and no !important — source order decides, so ordering is the override mechanism.

render.title: Skia rendering
render.body: A CPU raster surface, reused across frames, presented through softbuffer. The raster path is deliberate: it keeps rendered bytes deterministic, which is what makes the pixel tests possible.

events.title: Events and input
events.body: Click, input and explicit payloads, hit-tested against paint order and stacking. Text fields get real caret geometry, editing keys, and cross-frame focus preservation.

cli.title: A developer CLI
cli.body: velox init scaffolds a project, velox dev watches and rebuilds, velox lint checks .vx files, velox add writes a new component. The dev server is a full process rebuild — not hot state replacement.

tooling.title: Editor support
tooling.body: Syntax highlighting for .vx in VS Code, Zed and Neovim, shipped in this repository.

crates.title: Six crates, independently usable
crates.description: Each crate has its own Cargo.toml and its own tests. Nothing in the list depends on the whole.
crates.locNote: Line counts measured from the source tree at the time of writing; they move.
crates.footnote: The renderer crate defaults to building nothing — you opt into a backend explicitly.

showcase.description: This is a real .vx file from examples/todo. The template, the reactive state, and the scoped stylesheet all live in one file — and the compiler turns it into ordinary Rust.

examples.title: Runnable examples
examples.description: Three example programs live in the workspace. Build and run any of them with one command.

counter.desc: Signals, computed text, v-model on a text field, and buttons wired straight to state methods.

nonGoals.title: What it does not do
nonGoals.description: Stating the boundaries plainly is more useful than a feature list that overreaches.

items.hotReload: No hot state replacement. velox dev watches files and performs a full rebuild and restart — editing a component restarts the process.
items.reconciliation: No virtual-DOM diffing in the render loop. The reconciler that once existed was removed; the loop is immediate-mode and compute_layout runs fresh each frame.
items.key: The :key attribute is a plain string attribute. It does not reorder, diff, or preserve state across a reorder.
items.media: Dark mode is app-level. There is no prefers-color-scheme and no var() — a theme is a class on the root plus literal palettes.
items.events: Three runtime event channels exist: on:click, on:click-payload and on:input. There is no general keybinding system yet.
items.gpu: No GPU backend. The render target is a CPU raster surface, on purpose, to keep rendering deterministic.

story.title: Why I built Velox
story.subtitle: A web developer's search for native GUI without the complexity

chapters.title: The problem
chapters.content: As a web developer, GUI development felt unnecessarily complicated. GTK, Iced, QML — each has completely different syntaxes and steep learning curves. Web development styling concepts don't translate: margin, padding, flexbox — none of it works the same way. Logic and UI are split across different files in different languages. Electron and Tauri are good options, but they rely on web technologies and webview rendering, which fails to deliver truly native experiences. Flutter is powerful, but it's class-based, written in Dart, and adds a massive learning curve for web developers.

chapters.title: The insight
chapters.content: Rust feels like the future of coding — memory safe by design. But GUI frameworks in Rust aren't stable enough yet. I love Vue — its syntax is simply beautiful. What if a web developer could write Vue-like code, with CSS-like styles, but have Rust's memory safety and Flutter-level rendering power underneath?

chapters.title: The solution
chapters.content: Velox gives you Vue's developer experience: single-file components, template syntax, reactive signals, scoped styles. Under the hood, it's pure Rust with Skia (the same engine behind Flutter) rasterizing to a native window. No browser, no DOM, no webview. You write familiar code; Velox handles the compiler, layout engine, CSS cascade, and GPU rasterization.

chapters.title: Win · Win · Win
items: Developer gets Vue-like syntax and zero learning curve
Application gets Rust's memory safety and native performance
Rendering gets Skia — the same engine powering Flutter
